chapter_name: Effects of Physical Activities on Human Body
learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the incredible transformations your heart, lungs, muscles, and brain undergo when you exercise regularly!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Regular exercise makes the heart stronger. It pumps more blood per beat (increased stroke volume), lowers resting heart rate, and improves blood circulation.
Your lungs get more efficient! Exercise increases 'vital capacity' (the maximum amount of air you can breathe out) and strengthens the diaphragm.
Muscles grow thicker and stronger (Hypertrophy). Exercise also improves muscle endurance, allowing you to work longer without getting tired.
Weight-bearing activities (like running or weightlifting) increase bone density, making bones stronger and preventing diseases like osteoporosis later in life.
Exercise improves reaction time, coordination, and balance. It also releases 'endorphins' (happy hormones) that reduce stress and anxiety.

fun_activity.title: ❤️ Check Your Pulse
fun_activity.instructions: Find your pulse on your wrist or neck. Count the beats for 60 seconds while sitting. Now, do 20 jumping jacks and count again. See how much harder your cardiovascular system is working!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate between short-term effects (sweating, high heart rate) and long-term effects (lower resting heart rate, muscle growth).
📌 Know the definition of 'Stroke Volume' (blood pumped by the heart per beat).
📌 Explain how exercise delays the onset of fatigue.
quick_recap: ⭐ An athlete's resting heart rate is usually lower than a normal person's because their heart is more efficient.
⭐ Exercise increases the size and strength of muscle fibers.
⭐ Physical activity strengthens the immune system and speeds up metabolism.
